headline: Restructuring charge weighs on margins as growth stalls
summary_short: Procter & Gamble's quarter ended June 30, 2026 diluted EPS fell 14.9% y/y to $1.26 on revenue of $21,204M (+1.5% y/y, roughly flat q/q), as a $0.16/share restructuring charge and margin compression (operating margin -220bp y/y to 18.6%) offset flat organic sales growth.
summary_long: Revenue of $21,204M was flat q/q and up 1.5% y/y; organic sales growth was 0% as pricing offset flat volume, with a 1-point currency and 1-point divestiture drag. Gross margin fell to 48.5% (-60bp y/y) and operating margin to 18.6% (-220bp y/y), driven by a $0.16/share restructuring charge under the FY26-27 productivity plan plus higher marketing and commodity costs, partly offset by productivity savings. Diluted EPS fell 14.9% y/y to $1.26 (core EPS $1.43, -3%); net income fell 15.8% y/y to $3,044M. Cash fell to $9,942M (-19.2% q/q); long-term debt eased to $22,842M. FY2027 guidance: +1% to +3% organic sales growth, +0% to +3% core EPS growth.

drivers.explanation: Q4 organic sales growth was flat; FY2026 organic sales grew 1%, which the release says was within original guidance despite a challenging macro environment.
Organic sales growth was 0%: volume in-line with year-ago, pricing in-line, mix neutral; net sales also carried a 1-point currency drag and 1-point divestiture drag.
Operating margin fell 220bp y/y to 18.6% (core -130bp to 19.5%) on a $0.16/share incremental restructuring charge and higher marketing and commodity costs, partly offset by productivity savings.
Core EPS (excluding the restructuring charge) fell 3% to $1.43; currency-neutral core EPS fell 5% to $1.41, indicating a small favorable currency impact this quarter.
Every segment cited productivity savings and/or pricing being more than offset by higher marketing investment, commodity costs, and unfavorable product mix.
